land.text: the Rif coast and the Nekor valley, granted to Salih I ibn Mansur by the Caliphate

predecessors.note: 'The emirate was founded in 710 CE by Salih I ibn Mansur through a Caliphate grant.' Cliopatria has no shape before 750.

land.text: the Rif around the Nekor river, taken by Yusuf ibn Tashfin 'during his conquest of the Rif'

successors.note: The city was destroyed 1080-1081; the Almoravid conquest of the Rif is undated on the Nekor page.

capitals.name: Temsamane
capitals.note: Infobox 'Temsamane (710-760), then Nekor (760-1015)'; 'the initial seat on the coast'. Coordinates are approximate (the Al Hoceima coast), no page gives them.

capitals.name: Nekor (Ajdir area)
capitals.note: Founded by Sa'id ibn Idris ibn Salih 'in 760 or 761' (Emirate page; the Nekor page says Idris ibn Salih founded it 'between 749 and 761'); on the river Nekor 'east of al-Hoceima... about 25 km inland'. Coordinates approximate.

correction.text: the 750 shape (the Nekor valley and Rif coast) for the years of the Umayyad client emirate: 'centered in the Rif area of present-day Morocco'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria starts in 750; the infobox gives 'Established 710' and 'Client state of the Umayyad Caliphate (710-750)'. No page gives a boundary, so the 750 outline is reused. The Berber Revolt page (740-742) does not mention Nekor.

7,368 km2 around the Nekor valley and the Rif coast; the infobox gives no area. The page says 'centered in the Rif area', with coastal ports (Badia, Buquya, Balish) that 'paid taxes' and Ghomara and Sanhaja converts, so the outline is plausible but not checkable (unverified: page budget).

7,040 km2, the 750 shape trimmed where the Idrisids touch. The Idrisid page: at Idris II's death in 828 the principalities of Sijilmasa, Barghawata and Nekor 'remained outside their control'; Muhammad's brother 'Umar 'ruled over the Sanhaja and the Ghumara in the Rif region' (828-836). No Idrisid conquest of Nekor is recorded.

6,989 km2, trimmed where Cliopatria's Fatimid shape touches (922-925). The page has the Fatimids only as raiders ('sacked the city twice, in 917 and in 934'), not as rulers of the emirate; the trim is a Cliopatria artefact of overlapping neighbours.

7,040 km2, the Idrisid-neighbour outline again. 927: Abd al-Rahman III 'began his policy of defensive expansion by occupying Melilla' (Emirate page); the page does not say Melilla was Nekor's, so no border change is recorded.
6,989 km2. The 931 sack by Musa ibn Abi'l-Afiya and the 934 Fatimid sack are raids on the city, not changes of the emirate's land.
7,040 km2. The infobox lists Jurthum ibn Ahmad as emir 947-970; no territorial event on the page.

6,813 km2, trimmed against Cordoba's shape (980-1014). The Idrisid page: Buluggin restored Fatimid overlordship in the western Maghreb in 979 and was defeated by an Umayyad general in 985; it does not mention Nekor, so the Cordoba relation of these years is unverified (the Caliphate of Cordoba page was only a maintenance notice).

7,368 km2, the full 750 outline once Cordoba's neighbour shape ends. 'About 1015', Ya'la ibn al-Fatuh of the Azdaja tribe 'gained control of the emirate': a change of ruling line, not of land (rename event).

7,368 km2 for 1018-1027. Cliopatria stops in 1027, but the Emirate page has Ya'la's descendants holding power until Yusuf ibn Tashfin destroyed the city in 1080-1081, so the next keyframe carries the outline to 1081.

correction.text: the 1018 outline held by the Azdaja line of Ya'la ibn al-Fatuh until the Almoravid destruction of Nekor in 1080-1081

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has nothing after 1027. The page: Ya'la's 'descendants held power until' the city was destroyed 'in 1080-1081 for the fourth and last time by the Almoravid leader Yusuf ibn Tashfin' (the infobox, by contrast, says 'disestablished 1015'). The outline is unchanged; the page gives no territory for 1028-1080.

region.text: the Nekor valley and the Rif coast, 'centered in the Rif area of present-day Morocco'

ledger.note: 710: Salih I ibn Mansur founds the emirate of Nekor in the Rif. 'The emirate was founded in 710 CE by Salih I ibn Mansur through a Caliphate grant'; first seat Temsamane on the coast.

region.text: the Rif emirate as a client of the Caliphate

ledger.note: 710-750: client of the Umayyad Caliphate. Infobox: 'Client state of the Umayyad Caliphate (710-750)'.
750: the Umayyad overlord falls and the emirate stands alone. The year is the infobox's end of the client status; the page does not describe how it ended.
760: the seat moves from Temsamane to Nekor. Infobox 'Temsamane (710-760), then Nekor (760-1015)'; Sa'id ibn Idris ibn Salih founded Nekor 'in 760 or 761'.

By 931: Nekor a client of Cordoba. Musa ibn Abi'l-Afiya 'attacked and vanquished the Umayyad's vassal, al-Mu'ayyad, the Salihid ruler of Nekor', after Abd al-Rahman III began 'defensive expansion by occupying Melilla' in 927. The page does not say when the vassalage began; 931 is the year it is first attested.

region.text: Nekor, besieged, sacked and burned by Musa ibn Abi'l-Afiya

ledger.note: 931: Musa ibn Abi'l-Afiya sacks Nekor. 'Besieged, sacked, and burned Nekor in 931'; the Umayyads also sent 'a fleet of forty vessels' from Ceuta. The page does not say Musa held the land afterwards.
The page gives no end to the fighting: the emirate is back under its Salihid line (emirs 947-970 in the infobox). The year is a bridging judgement, one year after the sack.

region.text: Nekor, sacked by the Fatimids in 934

ledger.note: The page does not say when the Cordoban vassalage ended; 934 is the next dated event ('Fatimid troops sacked the city twice, in 917 and in 934'). Treat the 931-934 tint as a gap for a later page (Salihid dynasty; Umayyad Cordoba in the Maghreb).

About 1015: the Salihid line gives way to Ya'la ibn al-Fatuh of the Azdaja tribe. 'The Salihids held Nekor until about 1015, when Ya'la ibn al-Fatuh of the Azdaja tribe gained control'; the infobox gives 'disestablished 1015', but his descendants hold power to 1080-1081, so the colour continues.

region.text: Nekor and the Rif around the river

ledger.note: 1080-1081: the Almoravids take Nekor. The city was destroyed 'in 1080-1081 for the fourth and last time by the Almoravid leader Yusuf ibn Tashfin' (Nekor page: 'during his conquest of the Rif'). The pages date the city's destruction, not the end of the emirate.

region.text: the emirate's last land, destroyed by the Almoravids

ledger.note: 1081: the emirate of Nekor ends with the destruction of its city. Cliopatria ends it in 1027.

wars.name: Viking raid on Nekor (859)
belligerents: Vikings (859 expedition to Spain and North Africa)
wars.outcome: The Vikings, after Seville and Algeciras, 'plundered the city for eight days' and defeated a force that tried to stop them; no change of land.
wars.note: Nekor page: 'In 859, a major long-distance Viking expedition... plundered Nekor and defeated a Muslim force there.'

wars.name: Fatimid sacks of Nekor
wars.outcome: Fatimid troops sacked the city in 917 and again in 934; the emirate survived.
wars.note: The page names no Fatimid commander and no land change. The Idrisid page has the Miknasa, acting for the Fatimids, attack Fes in 917, the same year.

wars.name: Musa ibn Abi'l-Afiya's campaign against Nekor

zones.text: Nekor and the Rif coast, with Melilla occupied by Abd al-Rahman III in 927

wars.outcome: Abd al-Rahman III occupies Melilla (927); Musa defeats the Umayyad vassal al-Mu'ayyad and sacks and burns Nekor (931).
wars.note: From 927 to 929 Abd al-Rahman III also opens talks with the Idrisids (Emirate page); Musa switched to the Umayyads in 931 and was defeated by the Fatimid general Humayd in 933 (Idrisid page).

wars.name: Almoravid conquest of the Rif
wars.outcome: Yusuf ibn Tashfin destroys Nekor in 1080-1081 'for the fourth and last time' during his conquest of the Rif.
wars.note: The Nekor page: 'destroyed the city during his conquest of the Rif'; no other campaign detail.

certainty.note: A Rif tribal emirate with no surveyed or treaty frontier on any page opened; the outline is Cliopatria's approximation of the Nekor valley and coast.

sources.title: Emirate of Nekor
sources.note: Identity, 710 founding, capitals, 859, 917/934 Fatimid sacks, 927 Melilla, 931 Musa, c.1015 Azdaja, 1080-1081 Almoravid destruction. No infobox area.

sources.title: Idrisid dynasty
sources.note: 828 Nekor outside Idrisid control, 'Umar in the Rif, 917-985 Fatimid and Umayyad swings; no mention of Nekor itself.

sources.title: Nekor
sources.note: The city: founded 749-761, Vikings 859, destroyed 1080 during the Almoravid conquest of the Rif.

sources.title: Berber Revolt
sources.note: Thin for Nekor: the page does not mention it; 740-743 context only.

sources.title: Caliphate of Cordoba
sources.note: Thin: the page loaded as a maintenance notice with no North Africa content.

notes: Disagreements: the page's infobox has Nekor 'Established/Disestablished 710 / 1015' and Cliopatria 750-1027, but the Emirate page says Ya'la ibn al-Fatuh 'gained control of the emirate' about 1015 and his descendants held power until Yusuf ibn Tashfin destroyed the city in 1080-1081; the dossier follows the text (end 1081) and records 1015 as a rename. The city's founding is 'between 749 and 761' (Nekor page) or 'in 760 or 761' (Emirate page). The Salih I ibn Mansur article would not load (URL_NOT_FOUND for Salih_I_ibn_Mansur_al-Himyari); the page budget (5) went to the Emirate, Idrisid, Nekor, Berber Revolt and Caliphate of Cordoba pages, the last two giving nothing on Nekor. Cliopatria's shape changes are small trims against neighbours (Idrisids 793-921, Fatimids 922-925 and 936-946, Cordoba 980-1014) that no page confirms; each is reviewed ok. Not settled: whether the 927 occupation of Melilla took Nekor land; when the Cordoban vassalage (attested 931) began and ended; the Azdaja line's relation to Cordoba or the Zirids 1015-1081; who ruled Nekor 710-1015 beyond the partial emir list (Salih I to 749, Jurthum ibn Ahmad 947-970; no ruler strip written). A Salihid dynasty / Azdaja page would fix these. Names the gazetteer lacks: Temsamane and Nekor (places), the Rif (region); the shape is named through Cliopatria references instead. Coordinates of the two capitals are approximate, from the page's descriptions.
